title: Autocreate playbook links and trace snippets in incident channels
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
Many on-call alerts create noisy incident channels in Slack and manual triage requires hunting down the most recent runbook, relevant traces, and related dashboards. This slows median time-to-detect and time-to-resolution, and leads to duplicated context in postmortems.

Goal:
Automatically populate incident channels and PagerDuty incidents with: 1) one-click links to the canonical runbook/playbook for the alert (if available), 2) a short trace context snippet (trace id + span summary + link to traces UI), and 3) quick links to latency/error dashboards and recent anomalous metrics. The population should be deterministic, respect RBAC/privacy, and be extensible for future automation (e.g., auto-annotated postmortems).

Scope / Non-goals:
- In-scope: PagerDuty and Slack channel message enrichment at alert-create or escalation time; console/controller components to map alert metadata -> runbook; safe sampling of trace snippets (no PII); small UI affordance in Console to preview message.
- Out-of-scope: full postmortem generation and writing, replacing human triage decisions, or deep automated mitigation playbooks in this ticket.

High-level approach:
1) Extend alert enrichment pipeline to attach `playbook_id`, `trace_id_samples`, and `dashboard_links` to the incident payload emitted to integrations.
2) PagerDuty integration: when an incident is created, push a contextual note with the runbook link and compact trace snippet; include an Actions button linking to Console trace view.
3) Slack integration: auto-post a templated message into the channel that includes runbook link, a 1-2 line trace summary (service, span, error), and dashboard links; allow a one-click "Attach trace snapshot" that pins a short JSON summary.
4) Console: add an admin mapping table to associate alert signatures with canonical playbooks and preferred dashboards (editable by PM/On-call owners).

Security and privacy:
- Trace snippets must be redacted to remove user identifiers and payloads. Sampling heuristics must avoid sensitive spans (DB queries containing PII).
- KMS/encryption not required for pointers/URLs but access to traces/dashboards is enforced by existing RBAC. Integration messages must not leak internal tokens.

Acceptance criteria:
- For a test alert (load-test-alert-202503), when it fires, a Slack channel message is created with: runbook link, one trace id with service/span/error summary, and two dashboard links.
- PagerDuty incidents created from alerts include the contextual note within 30s of incident creation.
- Message templates render correctly for alerts with and without an associated playbook (fallback text shown).
- Trace snippet redaction verified on sampled traces (no PII).
- Manual QA checklist in Console and a short alpha rollout to Platform SRE.

Implementation tasks (high level):
tasks: Design message templates and variable interpolation (PM/Design review)
Extend alert enrichment pipeline to include playbook_id and trace snippets (backend)
PagerDuty integration: add contextual note push and action links (integration service)
Slack integration: implement channel message post + pinning option (integration service)
Console: mapping UI for alert -> playbook/dashboard and preview (frontend)
Tracing: add redaction and snippet extraction util (tracing infra)
Add unit/integration tests and end-to-end smoke test for sample alert
Create rollout plan + SRE alpha checklist and runbook update
